children: Next week’s key macro focus is Friday’s U.S. nonfarm payrolls report, including payrolls, the unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings, which are directly tied to the Federal Reserve’s rate path and are an important labor reading ahead of the October policy meeting. According to ChainCatcher, Wednesday at 8:15 PM will bring U.S. September ADP employment data, followed by the August core PCE price index year-over-year reading at 8:30 PM; Thursday at 8:30 PM will bring weekly initial jobless claims for the week ended September 26, and Friday at 8:30 PM will bring September seasonally adjusted nonfarm payrolls and the unemployment rate.

On the policy front, Bank of England Governor Bailey is scheduled to speak at 4:00 PM on Thursday, followed by European Central Bank President Lagarde at 9:30 PM. According to ChainCatcher, Federal Reserve speakers will be active from early Wednesday, including Chicago Fed President Austan D. Goolsbee, a 2027 FOMC voter, and St. Louis Fed President Alberto G. Musalem, a 2028 FOMC voter, while New York Fed President John C. Williams, a permanent FOMC voter, will deliver a keynote speech at the University at Buffalo. On Thursday, Fed Governor Lisa Cook, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, and Richmond Fed President Thomas I. Barkin are also scheduled to speak, and Williams and Dallas Fed President Lorie K. Logan will have public appearances on Friday.

In U.S. equities, Micron will report earnings after the close on Wednesday, and Nike will release its latest quarterly results on Thursday. The two reports are expected to offer signals on memory chips and consumer demand.

title: U.S. Jobs Report, Fed Speeches, and Micron Earnings Highlight Next Week's Macro Calendar
